sub_scenario.one_line: landscape architect: mornings and rotation, not continuous midday exposure

dialogue.content: I spent the first hour tidying the site diary and closing stale entries.
Anything still open?
Two items, both with owners.
The inspection schedule review wrapped early today.
Any surprises in it?
None worth recording.
Morning site visits, even long ones, have never triggered anything.
Mornings are unconditionally safe.
Unconditionally, per two summers of diary.
Someone new shadowed me in the project site this morning.
Did that slow you down?
A little, but the questions were good ones.
I batched my replies about the pour sequences into one message before lunch.
Cleaner than drip-feeding answers.
Much cleaner.
My medication makes me heat-intolerant, and my site diary documents it: both full-day summer supervisions without shade rotation ended in dizziness and an early departure.
Two documented episodes, same conditions both times.
Same conditions, same result.
Full days on shaded or indoor sites are equally uneventful.
Shade is as protective as timing.
Either one suffices.
I archived last cycle's notes on the inspection schedule and set up the new folder.
A fresh start?
As fresh as these things get.
My prescribing doctor confirmed the heat sensitivity is a fixed side effect for as long as I am on this medication.
A stable constraint, not a passing one.
Stable for the foreseeable.
A vendor call about the site diary ran long but ended well.
Worth the time?
This one, yes.
I walked through the project site checklist with the new starter.
How did they do?
Careful and quick, a good sign.
Quiet afternoon; I cleared the backlog around the pour sequences.
A rare day.
I did not waste it.
I flagged a small inconsistency in the inspection schedule records and fixed it at the source.
Root cause or symptom?
Root cause, for once.
The stadium project requires continuous on-site presence through the July pours, midday included, and the shade structures are not scheduled until August.
Continuous midday exposure in the exact hazard window.
The exact window, for four straight weeks.
I sketched next week's plan for the pour sequences before leaving.
Ahead of schedule?
Ahead enough to sleep well.
Lunch walk, then a clean pass through the site diary updates.
Does the walk help?
It resets the afternoon.
The July pours are the project's critical path; supervision cannot be casually reassigned once staffing is filed.
The filing is effectively irreversible.
Effectively, yes.
I compared two options for the inspection schedule tooling and noted a mild preference.
Decision made?
Deferred until the trial ends.
I closed the week by updating the project site handover notes.
Anything unusual to hand over?
Blessedly little.
The staffing form asks about my site availability profile for the summer program. What does my record support putting down?
